free_tier.stated: Aggregator of about 60 partner offers, most of them software licences rather than compute. The compute-relevant ones in the live October 2026 list are: Microsoft Azure 'Free access to 25+ Microsoft Azure cloud services plus $100 in Azure credit. For students aged 18+'; Camber 'Free Camber Student plan while you are enrolled, including 40 CPU hours, 5 GPU hours, 50 GB of storage, and 50 agent messages per month'; Heroku 'a credit of $13 USD per month for 24 months'; MongoDB '$50 in MongoDB Atlas Credits'; Datadog 'Pro Account, including 10 servers. Free for 2 years'; GitHub Codespaces 'Free Pro level access to Codespaces to use anywhere in your account'; Deepnote 'unlimited basic machines with up to 5GB RAM and 2vCPU'.

chaining: The pack is the widest single aggregator found, but it composes with nothing for a user because verification is the single point of failure for all 60 offers at once.

limits.value: Nothing in the pack can be claimed until a human or automated review accepts enrollment documentation, and that single review gate covers all 60 partner offers at once, so one failure removes the whole bundle.

identity_cost.detail: student-status documents reviewed by the GitHub Education team: the application page requires that you 'Provide documents that prove your current student status', accepting 'A picture of your school ID with current enrollment date', a class schedule, a transcript, or an affiliation or enrollment verification letter, and where a school was previously verified by academic email 'future applicants from the same school must also use an academic email'. Validation lasts 2 years and must be revalidated. No card, hold, debit or prepaid term is stated.

evidence.proved: A student must 'Provide documents that prove your current student status', and the accepted documents are 'A picture of your school ID with current enrollment date', 'Your class schedule', 'Your transcript', 'An affiliation or enrollment verification letter'; the page adds that where the system detects prior applicants from a school verified by academic email, 'future applicants from the same school must also use an academic email'.

The live partner list as of this read, quoted per partner above; the compute-bearing offers are Azure $100, Camber 40 CPU hours and 5 GPU hours a month, Heroku USD 13 a month for 24 months, Codespaces Pro, Deepnote 2 vCPU and 5 GB RAM.

'All users must be actively verified as a student by the GitHub Education team'; 'Student validation lasts for 2 years, after which you will need to revalidate your student status'; 'Offers may not be redeemed multiple times'.

notes: Refutation of the headline program in this class. An earlier dossier record in storage/github-student-developer-pack already found the pack fails on storage quota, but recorded identity_cost as 'email' at 'reported' confidence; the vendor's own application page says the evidence required is enrollment documentation, which makes the identity cost institution and the verdict fails-identity rather than fails-quota. The three cheapest verification documents to produce would be a class schedule, a transcript or an enrollment letter, and a user holds none.
